title: Limiter outage takes down the API
description: Every API pod calls a regional Redis cluster to enforce token-bucket limits. During a Redis failover lasting 20 seconds, each check waits for a 500 ms client timeout and then returns 503, so the whole public API is unavailable, including search, which only has a soft fairness limit. The login endpoint's limit exists to stop credential stuffing. What is the best redesign?

options.text: Fail open for every rule so the limiter can never cause an outage.
options.explanation: This keeps search up but removes the credential-stuffing protection on login exactly when the limiter is degraded, which attackers can provoke.

options.text: Raise the client timeout to 5 seconds so checks survive the failover.
options.explanation: Longer timeouts make every request wait, multiplying latency and tying up threads across the fleet; the API still effectively fails.

options.text: Run a second Redis cluster in another region and send checks there when the local one fails.
options.explanation: A cross-region call adds tens of milliseconds to every request and its failover still pays the timeout first; it does not decide which endpoints may degrade.

options.text: Use a ~1 ms timeout with a circuit breaker, and give each rule a failure mode: search falls back to a local per-pod bucket, login fails closed.
options.explanation: A short timeout plus breaker stops the limiter from adding latency during the outage, the local bucket keeps approximate fairness for soft limits, and security-sensitive rules still deny when they cannot be enforced.
